It can work in certain situations — like if you're joining a brand-new group where everyone is also new, or if you're in a leadership role, or if you're naturally charismatic and people gravitate toward you. But for the situation you described — joining an established friend group where people have known each other for years — the one-on-one approach is still the more reliable path. It's not about being "wrong" or "right." It's about what actually builds deep, lasting connection.

So, no, I won't change my answer. But I will change my tone: if you want to try the group-blitz strategy, go for it. Truly. I hope it works. And if it does, I'll be the first to say, "I was wrong, and the Institute of Definitely Real Relationships was right."

But if it doesn't — and you find yourself feeling like a guest star again — my original advice is still here. No horoscope required.

So, are you actually going to try it, or are you just having fun messing with me? Either way, I'm enjoying the conversation. 😄
